It's a shame Alan Wake is longer available for retail or online purchase, due to "expiring music liscenses" (Thanks capitalism!) It's easily in the same class as any other Remedy title, and honestly, it's probably in a class above. What would be an inferior third-person shooter to their previous series, the Max Payne games, is instead a thrilling tale of cinematic suspense and character development. I am sorry I never looked into the series before now. It features great pacing, quality voice acting, passably good driving sections, and if nothing else, really satisfyingly loud gun sounds.The facial animations haven't aged well these past years, but that's hardly a major shortcoming.
You take the role of the titular character, a crime fiction writer from NYC with possibly the worst case of writer's block on record. Wake has come to Bright Falls, Washington with his photographer wife Alice on vacation, in an attempt to clear his head, but within hours finds his wife missing, his car wrecked, the cabin he was to stay in vanished without a trace and a week's time gone by with no memory of such to speak of. What's worse, a malign force now stalks him through the night, wielding the shadows themselves as its weapon.
The light is your friend in Alan Wake, and there is precious little of it to go around. As in Left 4 Dead and many other games, light sources often mark your path, and many of them not only function as checkpoints but quickly replenish your otherwise painfully slow to regenerate health. Your enemies are shielded by darkness itself, and only your trusty flashlight can strip their defense before you go for the kill, using the sorts of guns you'd find lying around a rural community: police revolvers, hunting shotguns and rifles. Also at your disposal are two kinds of flares and flashbangs, with one kind of flare being fired from a flare gun and acting in essence as a grenade launcher.
Mechancally, the game is fairly formulaic: You move from checkpoint to checkpoint, blasting bad guys and pushing the occasional switch or button to open a door or something that might as well be a door. But your enemies are dangerous enough, and the characters believable enough, that you forget you are going through the motions of an oughts-era console shooter- and yes, I know it orignally released in 2010. The episodic format of the game greatly helps with the pacing, and it has some really great twists, especially in the bonus episodes: however you think the plot might turn out when you begin, it will likely defy your expectations. It also ends up being a lot harder then it intially feels, even on the easiest difficulty you will have a lot of near misses and scrapes, and this I recommend for a first play through- Alan Wake actually suffers from some balancing problems and it's a little to easy to get completely overwhelmed in the blink of an eye and ruthlessly beat to death. The dodge move is essentially broken, largely working only when it wants to, and your sprint duration is extremely limited, ensuring that you will rarely have the opportunity to avoid a fight. On the other hand, you are often given more supplies then you think you need- this is because you actually need all of it, so don't be afraid to use a flashbang or flare whenever you are cornered, as you are likely to find more.
If you did not have the good fortune to get this game before it was pulled from the Steam store, I highly encourage you to dig up a used Xbox 360 copy or secondhand key if you can find one, as it is definately worth your time.

Mafie is not a great game. It's not even a good one. It's okay.
It's two years past (god, it turned out to be 3 already) we got GTA V and it's main competitors didn't capture what makes such games awesome.
It's a combination of interesting characters, fresh story and well though mechanics.
Unfortunately, Mafia 3 gets not more than 6 out of 10 on all of this points.
Characters are pretty stereotypical, considering ongoing political agenda. U got rough but means good black guy, you got sneaky and cocky CIA operative, you get couple italian, irish and black allies. And all of the enemies are sick♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥in one or the other way. Plus exactly one main character in each side is woman. 4/10
Story is also quite boring. Seen multiple times 'I'll revenge death of my close ones, while deciding weather i'm good or bad person'. Side quests are written pretty good. You get the feel of the era, but that's about it. Final twists are actually great, but they do not overcome all the boredome of 30+ hours (2 first hours and last one are good). 6/10
Mechanics is the worst here. It seems developers got lazy or cocky or put into position of rushing the game, so you basically have couple very boring things to do. Drive around, kill or kinda-kill-interrogate (shoot, until he knees, then hold one button, then actually kill him), do it 5-10 times, kill mini-boss (same as interrogation), do all of this twice, get district, assign it to one of your allies, get some quire irrelevant perk, do it all over again 8 more times.
And yeah, to maximize your profits you actually have to drive at least 18 times all across other end of the map, make routin kill of everyone around, get into the truck and slowly ride all the way back. Oops, 20 minutes just went out of the window 17 of which are dull driving. And there is no fast travel at all.
Finishers are dull, it feels like it's 15-20 of them. Stealth gets really boring fast. Takes too much time without getting things easier. You can just stay in distance and shoot everyone with best gun you have unlocked so far.
Ocassionally you get some interesting cutscene or minigame like boxing or untying yourself, but that's it. 3/10
And I get it. It's hard to develop a lot of new and fresh mechanics on every corner of the game. Learn from GTA then. Script some great missions over and over again. Put a bomb under car. Poision drugs. Wreck a train. Steal some fuel from airport. Swap cash for guns deal. Smoke out some people on a factory. Put some fun dialogues while you driving.
But you get nothing.
Game tries to be engaging, educational, eye-opening, atmospheric, dynamic, a bit of strategic and economical, a bit of RPG and raising some moral questions. Instead it turned out to be dull and cliched.
Don't waste your money or what's most important - time. Go play GTA or FarCry 3 if you still haven't.

"Spellforce" ist das mir einzige bekannte Spiel, dass RPG und Strategie so gut in sich vereint. Auf dieses Spiel kann eine ganze Menge Zeit verwendet werden, da man alle nur erdenklichen Kombinationen bei der Fertigkeitenwahl des Avatars probieren kann. Das Spiel hält dabei nicht nur epische Schlachten gegen Bosse offen, sondern ist sehr vielfältig, da den Spieler diverse Quests (Haupt-, sowie Nebenquests) erwarten, die Aufgaben an sich sehr spannend sind in Bezug zu ihrer Geschichte, aber auch nicht "nur rohe Aufgaben" eingebaut wurden. Die Graphik empfinde ich als sehr angenehm. (Ich bin allerdings auch kein sonderlicher Graphik-Fanatiker. Zudem sollte man das Alter des Spiels berücksichtigen.)
Das für mich Faszinierendste am gesamten Spiel ist und bleibt jedoch die Geschichte, die dahinter steckt. Sie ist sehr spannend und hält den Spieler bei der Rolle. SIe zieht sich zudem durch alle drei Teile von "Spellforce" (das Hauptspiel "The Order of Dawn" und die beiden Erweiterungen "Breath of Winter" und "Shadow of the Phoenix") durch, sodass die Geschichte von Teil zu Teil fortgeführt wird und die Story komplettiert. Es können jedoch alle drei Teile unabhängig gespielt werden, was ich aufgrund der faszinierenden Story nicht empfehle.
Daher kann ich nur sprichwörtlich sagen: "Das Spiel war und ist jeden einzelnen Penny wert." und kann es jedem nur empfehlen, sofern man etwas für das Genre offen hat.

If you are looking for a hard game, with deep complexity, and variability on mechanics, this is your game, this is the definite roguelike and the shooter with no weapons.

The almost exclusive character design from McMillen ornates the game like a gem, and every object included in the game is unique and distinct from the others, and all of them are into the game's main theme (coming from a game with 197 different uprades, this is really something).
The gameplay is unique as it can be beatable with no upgrades, though it'll be nigh-impossible for newcomers, game experience trial and error is expectable for almost everyone who doesn't know what to do with items, and it's something reminescent from old videogames and Super Meat Boy. Even being hard, it is rewarding, and the rewarding system involving death is a mechanic that makes the player want to play more, and get more rewards, dying more and getting closer to the end of the game.

While it certainly has its flaws, Spellforce is an old gem. The main campaign is lengthy, getting through it took me about 90 hours, the story is quite fascinating as well. The RPG part of game is well developed, there are lots of side quests that make exploration rewarding and encourage you to step away from the main storyline. Apart from the main character, you also control up to five different heroes. The RTS part is also cleverly designed - an army is tied to the monument of the respective race, which also provides you workers to build a base. The number of structures of each race is quite big and there is room for customization, as you acquire building and unit plans through exploration usually tied to the main storyline but at times leading you to places you would never think of checking out. The fact that the main character is a rune warrior possessing worker and hero runes also makes the RTS part slightly more believable than usual.
The game highly favours a warrior type of character (such a character is, at times, even able to solo entire areas) and you might find yourself struggling if you decide to play a mage. Nevertheless, there is a variety of interesting spells and magic branches for you to explore, inviting those who demand a bit of a bigger challenge to choose their own path. Your small party of heroes can potentially be more efficient and less time consuming than an army and one could argue that base building seems pointless at times, but that is up to the player to decide.
To name a few flaws as well, the AI seems to be amazingly stupid at times and the translation isn't that splendid - there are a few spelling mistakes and some inconsistency, an example being the area Frost Marshes, which is referred to in the game with three different names. Despite its flaws, the game is well worth checking out. If you're looking for a more simplified and friendlier experience, you might prefer the sequel, but I would definitely recommend this game to any fan of either genre. The platinum edition also contains two long and challenging expansions, which, in my opinion, makes it more than worth the price.

A great and one of the few hybrids of RPG & RTS games, this game contains the best of both worlds. The combat system/RTS part doesnt have a Rock-Paper-Scissors combinatiopn of units but a "throw em all to battle" type which means the stronger wins and no need for tactics. In the english version of the game (I've played both the german & english version) the voice casting is pretty bad because of small number of actors.Most of the game runs around your avatar, a custom hero which you create (similar to Dungeon Siege & Titan Quest). The campaigns are long (some people complain too long) and gripping offering a weight variety of quests and action in both the RPG and RTS parts of the game. The game also includes a free-game-mode where you can simply play with your avatar and have fun. The game has also tons of equipment, spells & weapons just like every RPG should. One of the best parts of the game is the skill tree which is very simple to understand but offers a weight choice for your character evolution. Some/many may experience the CD not working requiring it to be inserted every time you start the game but it can be fixed without any problems (You have many "how to fix" guides in the Steam Community) The game may also have some bugs, but I haven't had any problems. It says the game is NOT compatible with Windows 7 but it works well for me (I guess i'm lucky). I would recommend this game to any RPG/RTS player, but would advise to wait till their prices drop a little during a sale. You won't be disapointed in this game
+ Good hybrid (best of both worlds)

+ Character creation & evolution
+ Free-Game-Mode

Labyrinth Escape reminds me of the games I made when I was 16-years-old and fooling around with the Unreal Engine.
This game is an extremely lazy effort filled with what look like stock assets. The level design is made to deliberately kill the player multiple times under the guise of the game being difficult, when in reality it's simply there to pad out the experience.
The gameplay includes eight levels of mazes that the developer slapped together where you navigate a few rooms and shoot weird rubber bullets randomly until you find the secret door to the next area. The game advertises destructible walls when in reality they are just rectangles that have physics enabled when you shoot them, or sometimes not because the physics will randomly stop working.
Littered throughout these levels are bombs that look randomly placed in bunches and impede your progress. Avoiding the bombs is impossible in some areas as you will always manage to explode one no matter what. When your character dies you can just do the maze again but nothing respawns so all the bombs you exploded aren't there anymore. That isn't difficulty, that's just irritating and padding out a terrible experience.
The developer has been responding to people on forums and locking threads that say negative things about the game. Their defence to the negativity seems to boil down to the game having a very small target audience, which in their mind is why people so far dislike it.
That is incorrect, people dislike the game because it isn't good. Nothing in your game that you have designed is enjoyable to play. Fans of maze games will hate it, FPS players will hate it and puzzle game players will hate it. It's not because these people aren't your target audience, it's because you have no target audience along with your presentation via trailers and descriptions being terrible.
Sometimes harsh words are needed in order for people to understand, but from the looks of it and every other game this developer has released, they either don't care or are blind towards any criticism.
Overall, this game has nothing to offer anybody. It's poorly made and resembles something a high school student would create during their lunchbreak.

Remark prior to reading:
- I do not care for the hype- nor the hate-train. I judge as I usually judge: based on nothing but my own opinion.
I didn't pre-order and kept my distance from this one until my favourite Reviewer (Gamestar) finally convinced me, and I'm with them 100%.
I really liked "Shadows of Mordor" except his many shortcomings. And I'm not even a big Tolkien or Lord of the Rings-Fan. So I'm speaking purely gameplay-wise.
But Mordor left me "meh!" after like 10 hours. Those 10 hours were great, but after that it just went boring and repetitive.
The usual problem of the usual Ubisoft-"Formula" of totally uninspired "map-clearing".
But with "Shadows of War" they really removed those shortcomings. Mostly. I would have bet they relied on former success and just go for a quick cash-grab.
Every Meter (or foot) you'd take, there's something to do. And most often not just for the sake of having something to do, but for skill-points,
special skills or story or just moneyyyzzz.
And "recruiting" Captains to join your army, assigning them jobs, helping them complete missions, slowly raising your force to wage war in a region and all that is really motivating. And overall a damn fun to do!
But beside all the shining glory there's an UGH! behind it:
Loot-Boxes. Yes. Sucks. They should be quartered, hanged and burned for that. But who can blame them. I guess those boxes alone are flushing
at least a Million bucks into their cash-registers. So who wouldn't tread that path? (Except CD Project Red who simply did it with pure excellence)
*BUT* they are really not needed if you enjoy the game for the gameplay and not just for rushing through the story. The "Endgame" will be
hidden behind a "grind" (which is good if you actually enjoy the game, or else...why play it?) or a paywall. Legendary Orks will help, yes.
But finding them is the thrill. Just buying them. Meh. Probably gets boring very fast.
Normal loot-boxes with items or Orks up to Epic (one level below Legendary) are buyable with ingame-currency which is not hard to come by.
And if you're OK with that, you can even cheat your money and edit your Orks. IF you are ok with that and are in a rush.
(I only fear that these not-really-super-needed-loot-boxes are just slowly a test for our stupidity and will increase in necessity with every game. Let's hope not)
(!) SIDE-NOTE: If you really don't want loot-boxes or any online-content at all in your SINGLE-PLAYER-game, then simply decline
the TOS the FIRST(!) time you start the game (it's bound to your account and you cannot change it later!). You then have the total and complete
single-player-experience. No boxes, no revenges, no invasions.
If you liked Mordor, YES!
If you liked Mordor but don't want to invest time to see the end AND don't want to spend money? Nah.
IF you liked Mordor and don't care to see the end as long as you're having fun for 10, 20, 30 or more hours? Sure!
If you haven't played Mordor but like Action-RPGs with Stealth-mechanics (which you don't HAVE to use) like Dishonored? See above.
If you don't like the usual Ubisoft-"Formula" of clearing maps: Nah, maybe not.
Just be "warned": If you don't LIKE to spend many many hours in a game you enjoy, you will be forced to pay money to see the end, or you just don't.
Then again, who cares. The Story isn't THAT interesting anyway.

Been looking for a "relaxing" game? Oh, haha...hahahahaha...have WE got a game for YOU...
Mountain gives new meaning to the word "relaxing". It would also give new meaning to the word "game" if, erm...if I thought it actually qualified as one. As a persistent champion of all games borderline non-game-ish, even I have to concede that this maybe isn't one.
Let's analyse the basics. Is it interactive, in a way which movies and recorded music and printed books are not? Yes. Yes, it is. For starters, you can use the mouse to change your view of the mountain, so technically it does have "controls". What's more, you can also use some of the letter keys on your keyboard to play musical notes; which, upon rare occasion, cause something to "happen", like making the sky rain gold coins. Your chances of lucking upon this combination of keys is nigh-on non-existent, however, so unless you're the type who likes to Google obscure♥♥♥♥♥♥ this isn't really going to fulfil any desire for intuitive "gameplay". There's certainly no bona fide "puzzles" which I stumbled upon.
Does it have a story? Um...the story of a mountain slowly evolving, I suppose. Is that a story? Traditionally stories have "characters". Is the mountain a character? Um...dunno, normally characters have personalities, even when they're cartoon animals. I guess it has events, like changing weather conditions, so maybe we could stretch that out to say it has a "plot". Maybe. Sort of. But not really..?
I've seen people refer to Mountain as a mildly "interactive screensaver", and I'd say that's a fair call. I'd probably be most comfortable calling it an "experience", and as experiences go, it's certainly not an unpleasant one. Whether it will be one's idea of exciting or engrossing is another matter entirely.
Apparently, some people have spent tens or hundreds of hours on this thing. I don't think that will be happening to me. This is perhaps a little too close to a "walking simulator" - minus the actual WALKING part - for my tastes. I honestly need at least a SMIDGEN more interaction than this to feel that my time has been well-spent.
I'm still going to recommend it, if only barely, and only in acknowledgement that there are definitely people out there for whom this will be a worthwhile experience. Regrettably, I wasn't one of them. But an arguably quality product is still an arguably quality product, even if I didn't "get it". And I'm afraid that I really, REALLY didn't get it...
Verdict: 6/10.

Castle of Illusion is a great game.
I would even say it's one of the best platformers I've played this year.
You play as Mickey who has to save his beloved Minnie from an evil witch, and collect as many gems and other special items along the way. There are also special unlockable costumes for Mickey to be found as well.
The aesthetics are gorgeous, leaving us with a very colorful game. The music fits the mood very well. The narrator, as well as the voice actor for other characters, do a great job at their respective roles. The cutscenes are played out in a lovely 2D hand drawn style, almost like reading a story book.
And don't let the fact that it's a Mickey Mouse game catch you off guard. Castle of Illusion is in no way a game only kids would enjoy. There's plenty of challenge for all ages, especially if you're trying to 100% clear it.
Overall, it's a must play for any Disney fan, and even if you don't like Disney or Mickey Mouse too much, it's still worth a look.

Shadow of War is like a drug deal gone bad...
You bring the goods, and expect to receive a briecase full of money for your troubles, but when you open it to count the cash, you notice that half the money is in fact newspapers, and that's when the shots start getting fired...
And that's the whole thing really, Shadow of War is only half of a game. Don't get me wrong, it's an improvement on most aspects of the first game. The nemesis system has been improved, you have 5 different regions to explore, and for 4 of them you can use your dominated orcs to take and defend fortresses. You get new tools to play with in the form of skills and said skills also make it easier to exploit the weaknesses of your targets. The overall experience is more comfortable and more fun. It's not without flaws though, as the game often has troubles understanding where you want to go when you're climbing, a problem old AC games had, and which took them quite a few games to fix. I'm sure if you give them two more games, the guys behind the games will manage to make the climbing smooth. The same issue exists for the dodging, which is also the same key than the vaulting over ennemies, and which means the game has a lot of trouble trying to know if you want to dodge or jump over someone. I also question some choices of key bindings, such as the super sprint on the mouse wheel, and the fact azerty keyboards are unproperly supported(they are supported for regular controls, but as soon as you have some menus, or for some kind of collectible, they forget about it making it quite awkward).
So overall, it would still be a good game if it wasn't for a glaring flaw in the pacing of the story and the actual content. Game has four acts, and for all intents and purposes, it ends at act 2. Act 3 is just one big mission which is barely larger in length than any other mission, and during which the story pretty much reaches a half-baked conclusion with things left unclear, and a character doing a complete 180° in her personnality(I try to keep things as spoiler-less as possible). To give you an order of idea, doing 100% of everything up to the end of act 2 tooks me around 50+ hours of playing. Act 3, to be generous, is 30 minutes long...
This is not how you pace your story. No matter what you do, you separate your story in order to make sure it flows nicely, and you do so in such a way parts are roughly equal if not in length, at least in intensity and progression. Act 3 could pretty much not exist, and be part of Act 2, and no one would notice.
And then, you have the infamous Act IV... Act IV is part filler, part post game content. It's basically a serie of 10 fortress defenses of increasing difficulty just to unlock the final ending which is 3 minutes long. It's a boring and tedious process made even worse by the fact you are starved for xp, and that your level is used as a cap for the maximum level your orcs can have. Not only that, but the only way to level your orcs at a proper speed is to send them to pit fights which you can only watch. So basically, while you level them, you are deprived of player agency, and forced to endure watching the fights over and over. And even if they sometimes can be cool and funny, there is a limit to what you can stomach without wanting to actually play the game. Basically, the game expects you to not be able to defend your fortress, and lose, because then retaking it will give you the xp you desperately need. Problem being, retaking the whole thing is a long and lengthy process which you already did at least 5 times at that point. It doesn't bring anything new to the table, you don't have any story elements to actually push you forward and motivate you. It's just a whole bunch of nothing. Out of context xp grind like some kind of MMO.
It's like a soufflé which deflates to pitiful levels when you cut in it. Of the four acts drama, there are only two, the prologue and the actual game. It feels like the funding and creative efforts were completely cut mid developpement.
I don't recommend the game at any price over maybe 25 euros top. Likely in the amount of 20, as I consider that's what it's worth.
It's fitting in a way, that half the game is actually fleshed out, and the other half, is in fact, a wraith of what could have been.

Bought this game during a gameplay drought.
I stumbled upon it and thought, "Hey, muddin' game."
The game is visually satisfying.
Here's how the game works:
Get 'X' amount of logs to the objective. You have 5 maps to pick from (they recently just added one).  I have a choice of a Jeep or a rear wheeled drive pick up truck.  The jeep can carry a small amount of repair points known as a trunk, and the truck can carry logs a small amount of logs (not enough for one trip).  I take the jeep and start muddin' my way through the terrain.  The map is blocked by 'fog of war' and can be unlocked by driving up to fog unlocks, which will reveal portions of the map.  From here you can see other trucks spread thoughout the map that can be unlocked by driving up to them. Bigger trucks.  Bohemoths that can traverse the thickest of mud.  You find one and unlock it, but the engine wont start because it's too damaged.  This is where you would use the trunk from the jeep and apply it to the new rig, but it won't fix the whole thing, only patch it. So know I have to limp this thing back to start, which will always be a garage.  From here it will automatically fuel and repair your rigs.  Depending on the rig, you can change what you haul, from an empty fuel cistern that can be filled at a gas station on the map, to a garage trailer that can be placed on a garage point, or a long log trailer that takes the maximum amount of logs to the objective.   You see, the objective is easy, gathering the resources to complete the objective is where the gameplay is at.
Recently the devs have started working on this game again, which is AWESOME!  This game has soooo much potential.  This is one of those games I like to come back to with my friends and mess around.  It kinda reminds me of Top Gear.

A surprisingly good Platforming/Action side-scroller that sort of came out of nowhere.
Dust takes what it lacks in raw weapon and attack variety, and makes up for it by having an extremely fluid combo system and effective chain building between your sword and special projectile attacks (Fired by your floating, wise-cracking companion).   Trading off swings and a "Whirlwind" attack with your sword, with sucking up projectiles to fire massive volley attacks at your foes.    Attack with the sword to build charge, clear the screen with Whirlwind+Magic attacks.
Combat aside, the game features a better story than one might expect from a platformer/brawler.  Numerous likeable characters dot your path through the game, facing your character with conflicts and suppressed memories as you progress through to discover your past.   The personalities you encounter throughout the game range from serious and heartfelt, to light hearted and wise-cracking (See your companion)--Offering a good balance of good times and bad.
The game's story and side quests should give you 12-15 hours depending on how skilled you are; Fleshing out to 20 or so hours if you decide to go on a collection spree, and wish to complete the various (Optional) challenges in the game.  Exploration is rewarded with better gear, which essentially equates to stat upgrades.
As a PC port the game excels, having a slew of graphics options and offering uncompressed sprites/cutscenes for better quality.   I've been told it plays well on KB+M, but personally found a controller more favorable.    Having purchased the game at launch, I felt it was worth full price and potentially even more. One of my more enjoyable gaming experiences this year.
PS: If for some reason you're avoiding the game because you see "Ew Furries", well, you're missing out on a quality game and that's your loss. It's stylized in a cartoony manner and appeals with very friendly character personalities.

Let me begin by first congratulating you on clicking this wonderful game. Kudos to you. Let me next congratulate you for looking at the reviews of this game, as rightly you should. Now let me slap you in the f*cking jaw for clicking on "Negative Reviews".
Entrance a little too strong? Well consider it a wake up call.
If you have played many an RPG and completed it with a lingering craving for depth and lore, then this game is your healing salve. This game has some of the richest storytelling I have ever had the pleasure of being part of, paired with it's sheer beauty and somewhat impressive mod support, you can not go wrong with this purchase.
The voice acting is on point, similar to that of Fable, with its regional 'Typically British' dialect which is laced with humour and one-liners. The gameplay, whilst some suggest is 'clunky', works well considering the type of game this is. The graphics are demanding, but if you have the power to run this at high settings, they will leave you awestruck. The storyline is fresh and cleverly written (with enough room for plenty of side quests), and although it seems typically linear, the areas you visit are open enough to allow you to breath.
The game is without a doubt targetted at a more mature audience, with an abundance of nakedness particularly from the female cast (which is brilliant for us single men - am I right?!) as well as a great deal of 'curse' words throughout. I can not say exactly how to play this game, nor can I elaborate on how much you will enjoy it - you quite literally just have to sit down and indulge its richness and take your time, let yourself break away from the quest grinding, go explore, talk to NPC's, loot houses, do some crafting... whatever it is you take delight in, just... do it.
Its simple, and your decision to purchase this game should be too. The negative reviews that flood this page genuinely are talking out of their ars*s, their play time alone is enough to suggest they havent actually PLAYED the game. They have obviously gotten past the tutorial and cried because everything wasn't handed to them on a silver plate.
For roughly the 6th time now I've seen this game go on sale for less than £5... If you are worrying about "wasting" £5 then you have issues. Seriously, you could find that on the street. Or you could go busking for an hour, whatever.
Buy it.

One of the best Indie games out there!!!
First off the music in this game is AWESOME! A great 80s style music makes this game even much more enjoyable to play. I highly recommend you buy the soundtrack cause the developers deserve it for making an amazing soundtrack.
Gameplay: This game is straight up difficult. You need to have fast reaction times since enemies move really fast and attack you quickly. Your objective is to eliminate all the enemies on each floor to complete the level. All enemies die in one shot, but the twist is that you are the same exact way! Before each level you get to choose a mask that will give you different abilities and each level has certain masks that are well suited for each other. Not to mention this game is violent, ya its all pixelated but the kill animations makes this really violent.
Story: The story for this game is really dark and interesting. You are a no-named character that is getting phone calls that essentially leads him to killing off the russian mob. While doing so you see this hallucinations of 3 characters that question who you are and if what your doing is worth it kinda of thing... In the end if you sit back and look at how the story is going, its really interesting and a good way of storytelling IMO.
Conclusion: Hotline Miami (as well as its sequal) is one of the best Indie games out there. The gameplay is very tense and a lot of fun. And the soundtrack will be one that you will listen too for a while and eventually will play in your car lol.
Rating: 10/10

This review comes from a Platinum God a.k.a. 100% of the game completed
If you are looking for a hard game, with deep complexity, and variability on mechanics, this is your game, this is the definite roguelike and the shooter with no weapons.
The story is deep and grim, at the same time that it isn't really told by anyone as the game progresses, but with simple ~30 sec animations you get a glimpse of what really happens while the game passes. The almost exclusive character design from McMillen ornates the game like a gem, and every object included in the game is unique and distinct from the others, and all of them are into the game's main theme (coming from a game with 197 different uprades, this is really something).
The gameplay is unique as it can be beatable with no upgrades, though it'll be nigh-impossible for newcomers, game experience trial and error is expectable for almost everyone who doesn't know what to do with items, and it's something reminescent from old videogames and Super Meat Boy. Even being hard, it is rewarding, and the rewarding system involving death is a mechanic that makes the player want to play more, and get more rewards, dying more and getting closer to the end of the game.

I played the original Half-Life mod a lot back in the day, and this sequel improves the original in every way. This game is living and breathing, and there are tweaks and new content almost every week. The gameplay pits aliens and space marines against each other on a variety of well-made maps.
At first glance, this is a first-person shooter, but there's more depth than that. Each side has a commander with a top-down view of the battlefield. Commanders can build structures, order their troops, and provide certain powers and benefits to their team. The two teams are vying for resource nozzles, which provide a stream of personal and team resource points to be spent on upgrades, weapons, and evolutions.
Each side has a unique tech tree, with the marines gaining things like motion sensors that can track aliens through walls, and mechanized suits with lots of firepower. The aliens have 5 different lifeforms to evolve into, as well as a variety of abilities, like cloaking, regeneration, and teleportation. Each lifeform plays differently, so there's a lot of room for specialization.
In short, this is a well-made game with fantastic visuals and fast-paced strategic gameplay. Being a part of a coordinated team is really something special in this game. I can't reommend it enough.

SpellForce.. this game, almost perfection
>Game Description
To start, SpellForce is a rather well done hybrid of an RPG and an RTS, with both aspects of the game being rather good. Most of the game revolves around your hero, who is a ''Rune Warrior'', and has the ability to activate different types of monuments and such, which are able to summon Avatars, who are weaker heroes, but a force to be reckoned, especially in RPG maps. You're also able to activate monuments of different races, which are able to summon a specific race's workers or warriors(presuming you meet the requirements). Summoning workers or Avatars also consumes
your rune power, which determines the rate at which the workers or Avatars are summoned, and recovers slowly. Now, for the RTS part, it is combined with the RPG part, as you need to find blueprints to be able to build more advanced buildings or units, and you must also find worker runes to increase the power of your units. The game has 3 lenghty campaigns, and a free play mode. As for me, I'm playing the free play mode currently, where you have free choice of what map you play, or what race you play.
Pros : +Lenghty campaign
+Well-done hybrid of RTS and RPG
+Half-naked women in loading screens
+Plenty of hero customization
Cons : -Somewhat bad translation
-Spells require you to find a higher level scroll to level up
-Walking from one part of the map to another can get tiring at times
[8.5/10]

First of all, I am really into game design not so much spelling. But none the less, off of my recomendation I have already gotten four other people to buy this game (I never, never, give undue praise). This is the first Steam review I've ever bothered to publish. But given the current climate and cultural momentums in the gaming industry this review is warrented. From the raw volume of content in the base game, Monolith Productions have put other game developers to shame; for taking  content in their games and breaking it up into DLC's, even a potential sequal, and still have less content than you get with volume of playable material just with the base game of Shadow of War.
IT IS ALMOST LIKE THEY LISTENED TO THE COMMUNITY AND REMIDYED ALL IRRETATING ELEMENTS OF THE GAME'S PREDICECOR AND IMPROVED BOTH THE BREATH AND DEPTH OF WHAT MADE THE EXISTING GAME A MASTER OF WHAT IT AIMED TO ACHIEVE. As of over 50 hours into the game I am still not even near the end of story content available
Only Three Gripes
-Talion is seemingly the worlds greatest acrobat now (but ok I can overlook realism for magic so this is nothing). Still this takes some weight out of objects being physically far apart within the game world with how easy it is to traverse large distances.
-Some frustration with controling the actions and camera angles ONLY WITHIN small spaces that are saturated with alot of NPC's.
-Not an ideal way to navigate the various maps scales (but still huge credit to their first aim at implimenting this map navigation system). Simply said though, you will get used to it after some playtime.
Main Three Remedies to disliked elements
-in battle actions taking too long by speeding them up so that combat flows smoothly and is exciting
-game world scope feeling somewhat small after you understand the general layout by instead using strategic map layout to increase the ammount of intricacy verticly and horizontaly. As well as create more (over twice as many) playable maps.
-two dimensional story progression and skill trees were made to be dynamic enough that you really feel like you are in an open world.
Main Three Enchancments
-the nemisis system has, I dare say, doubled or more accuratly, trippled in depth and scope or uruk uniquness. As well asthe ammount of dynamic actions that can occur within the game world. It truely feels like a political thriller within a video game.
-the ability to have a skill tree that is customized to the player's play-style such that your shadow of war game will feel different than if you try playing on your friend's PC. This helps you feel much more immersed in the game since you need to meet the game's goals however you best are able to. Note: it is still well balanced in my opinion.
-Post story gameplay still ccarries an open world atmosphere with content that can acctualy entertain you beyond collectables (I'm looking at you EA Games). This goes to show just how much depth there is built into the game's systems not just its story.
I could go on with multitudes of reasons why this game is one of my top 5 games ever in my lifetime collection of over 110 games across six (yes six) different consoles since I started gaming when I was a little kid. (I'm in my 20s don't get any ideas I'm not as old as that sounds)
For every other developer that wants to know how you make an open world RPG. Here it is. This is how you make a high quality gameing franchise of this genre in this day and age. Also, I will not forget to give credit to Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment for not over promising on the game when it was marketed. Thank you for actually giving a realistic protrail of the game's experience that is still awsome.
So in short, buy the damn thing.

This review is based on the game as it came at the time I bought it (a few days ago) including all updates and patches that it would've had at that time.
If you like the concept of this game and enjoy simulators then I doubt this game will disappoint. The graphics are gorgeous. The way the vehicles cut through the mud, brush past trees and slosh through water is all done superbly. I have never known another game that comes even close to simulating ground deformation in this way. The more you drive the tracks in big trucks, the more tricky sections can become churned up, giving you increasing challenges to get through. The level of detail on the vehicles is brilliant - swinging ropes, moving running gear, smoke and heat effects - it's all there. Although one thing that isn't there is any drivers. It seems a shame that in such an immersive simulator as this, the trucks appear to be just driving around magically by themselves. In terms of game-play, having a certain number of 'drivers' to use per map might have been a nice touch, but it's still a fantastic game even with innumerable invisible drivers.
There's no music and it doesn't need any. The sounds of the vehicles are spot on. The roar of the really big diesel engines is throaty and satisfying, the transmission whines on the little Uaz truck and the thudding and clunking as you crawl over rough terrain is just right. The ambient sounds are also great. It's a bit like a sounds of nature relaxation CD (until you fire-up a truck of course).
The maps are all very similar in visual appearance and there are no weather effects, just day & night, but each contains unique challenges.
Within minutes of playing the game I hated the two camera views. The fixed 3rd person view seems useless, most of the time all you can see in this view is the back of the truck. The mouse-controlled view is the one to use, but it seems to be anchored to the truck in a strange place so it rotates awkwardly, it doesn't zoom out far enough, and when you do zoom out it automatically zooms back in again after a few seconds. Within hours of playing the game, I'd got used to the awkward camera angle and reconciled that when you're off-roading, you don't get to see all around the vehicle, or which way the steering wheels are turning etc. After continued playing the camera angle bothers me far less, but it would still be nice to zoom out more.
If you like driving big trucks off road and have perhaps longed for a game that effectively simulates mud when off-road driving (which I have), then this is possibly the greatest game ever made. There is plenty to do so long as you enjoy the concept - scouting the terrain to uncloak the map, locating, repairing and refuelling additional trucks, keeping all your trucks fuelled and repaired, towing and winch recovery, setting up new garages and collecting and delivering loads of timber. The two main styles of play I have found so far have been scouting in the small truck, which gives a 'trials' type off-roading experience, picking the best route across terrain with no tracks, finding gaps to wind through trees, pushing through scrub and wading through uncharted depths. Then there's the more 'convoy' style of driving. Perhaps taking a couple of log trucks and a fuel tanker along wide (or at least, the widest you can manage to find) forestry tracks, using the vehicles together to find the best routes and recover, winch and tow each other when needed (and trying not to get all 3 of them stuck).
However, if you just go out and drive in a truck to try and get from A to B, then auto-restore your vehicle back to the starting point if you crash and try over, you'll probably get bored quickly. I think you need to actually enjoy trying to recover stuck vehicles to appreciate this game, it's as much about vehicle recovery and problem solving as it is about driving.
Moving long trailer loads is a nightmare, and that's exactly how it should be. It's incredibly challenging and rewarding to take big curtain sided trailers or long loads of logs from A to B without spilling the load, inching forward and back at corners to get the right angle, winching up muddy inclines and nervously crawling through water crossings.
I don't even want to mention mods because this game is amazing without them, but I've gone and mentioned them now. Mods would be nice. It'd be nice to be able to add vehicles without them replacing existing vehicles in the game, and to get some new maps with a different look to them. But really, if you want to drive big trucks in mud, then this game allows you to just that, and it does so brilliantly.

Spintires is an excellent game.  I have gotten many hours of enjoyment out of it and I am going to get many more.  Once you get started playing this game, it is hard to stop.  The vehicles are fun to drive and the terrain is fun and challenging to navigate.  If you think you're on solid ground, you probably aren't and you will sink your truck to the axels.
This being said, I would still call this game a beta that is in its late stages.  The way the camera operates is horrible, the ingame menus are bad, and every update to the game erases your save data.  There have also been some issues between the community, Pavel (lead developer/creator) and Oovee.  At the moment, things seem to be sorted out and Oovee has promised more updates, features, and transparency but we will have to see.
In conclusion, if development on this game was halted today it is still a very fun and enjoyable experience.  I have played for almost 45 hours and I have not yet to even try the map added in the latest update.  The modding community is amazing and thriving at the moment.  Kind of treat buying this game as buying an early access game.  The development plan and future of this game is a little shaky at the moment.  So if development suddenly stops or major changes come to the game, be ready.  But overall, you will not be wasting your money and will have a great time playing this game.

text:
There is/has been a lot of drama happening between Oovee and their sole programmer half a world away for some time, now.  A recent update made the game unplayable.  A forum user who created a fix for the patch claims it was because of "timebombs" put in to intentionally cause the game to stop working.  As of 3/3/16, an update fixing the crashing has been put out and the game works normally.
--------
Spintires is a game that consists of a constant low-level challenge.  It's like a sleepy Mario Kart or Gran Turismo.  It's also similar in feel to Euro Truck Simulator 2.  You could definitely time-trial a map; maybe even race in MP informally.  But, I maintain it's a lot like playing skyrim and not doing quests.  Goes great with podcasts, too.
It's a good off-road sim.  The terrain deformation is realistic and detailed.  The vehicles (there are about a dozen right now) have varied capabilities and equippable modules.  From a Jeep to a monster 8x8.  There is fuel consumption and damage.  And, you can choose between a "casual" and "hardcore" difficulty.  Hardcore prevents you from resetting your vehicles to the garage and increases fuel consumption.  I play casual.  Once you get a load, that truck is kind of on a hardcore-lite; you can't reset it without losing your load and going back to square one.
There's also a pretty big mod scene on the Steam Workshop and in other places.  You can get trucks and maps.
And there is the 2013 tech demo if you want to test the game's performance on your rig.
All-in-all, a nice way to pass time and worth the price.  It seemed high to me initially but I'm still playing it and I'm not even crazy into playing it.  And, I've only tried SP.

I'm suprised that BTD Battles actually made it to Steam, and It works very well.
Although, it dosen't seem anymore different to the Mobile edition with some exceptions, such as a monkey hand for a cursor, using 1,2,3, etc. for hotkeys, upgrading ( , and . ) and some other features.
I remember when BTD Battles came out for FLASH, and everyone USED to play it on the Ninja Kiwi website. Till it came out for mobile, than nobody played the Flash version.
I REALLY like you can play this with the players on Steam and on an iPad/Android, so you'll not have to wait about 20 seconds to fight someone (unless you have really bad connection, if so, you shouldn't play this game).
And connecting to the Steam Cloud and the Ninja Kiwi Cloud, I found that really useful if you had a record before.
But of course, there are some problems.
I'm a bit dissapointed that if you want to have the best of BTD Battles, You'll need to pay for it, and the Club Rooms is a perfect example. I don't really wanna pay 5 USD (I'm Australian, so I'd have to pay more) just for new maps and different gamemodes.
And also slowly having to play for hours on end to unlock the best towers, it's gets quite frustrating that you want to unlock a 4th tier Bloonchipper, but if you're into the grinding genre of games, I guess it's alright...
Also, I would want to be able to customise hotkeys, but if that is not going to happen, it's ok, I guess. BUT there is no hotkeys to send out Bloons, and I'm REALLY used to do that. It's really weird.
Overall, I'm glad this went onto Steam, and I'll be playing it on Steam, the game itself is great, challenging and competitive. (I mostly wrote about the Steam and Mobile version and differences, sorry.) But I shouldn't be able to pay 6.40 AUD to have access to the more interesting features of the game.
Also, Hotkeys. Give me dem hotkeys man.

Let me begin by first congratulating you on clicking this wonderful game. Kudos to you. Let me next congratulate you for looking at the reviews of this game, as rightly you should. Now let me slap you in the f*cking jaw for clicking on "Negative Reviews".
Entrance a little too strong? Well consider it a wake up call.
If you have played many an RPG and completed it with a lingering craving for depth and lore, then this game is your healing salve. This game has some of the richest storytelling I have ever had the pleasure of being part of, paired with it's sheer beauty and somewhat impressive mod support, you can not go wrong with this purchase.
The voice acting is on point, similar to that of Fable, with its regional 'Typically British' dialect which is laced with humour and one-liners. The gameplay, whilst some suggest is 'clunky', works well considering the type of game this is. The graphics are demanding, but if you have the power to run this at high settings, they will leave you awestruck. The storyline is fresh and cleverly written (with enough room for plenty of side quests), and although it seems typically linear, the areas you visit are open enough to allow you to breath.
The game is without a doubt targetted at a more mature audience, with an abundance of nakedness particularly from the female cast (which is brilliant for us single men - am I right?!) as well as a great deal of 'curse' words throughout. I can not say exactly how to play this game, nor can I elaborate on how much you will enjoy it - you quite literally just have to sit down and indulge its richness and take your time, let yourself break away from the quest grinding, go explore, talk to NPC's, loot houses, do some crafting... whatever it is you take delight in, just... do it.
Its simple, and your decision to purchase this game should be too. The negative reviews that flood this page genuinely are talking out of their ars*s, their play time alone is enough to suggest they havent actually PLAYED the game. They have obviously gotten past the tutorial and cried because everything wasn't handed to them on a silver plate.
For roughly the 6th time now I've seen this game go on sale for less than £5... If you are worrying about "wasting" £5 then you have issues. Seriously, you could find that on the street. Or you could go busking for an hour, whatever.
Buy it.

Hotline Miami is a game that I picked up in the sales for less than £3 and I wished I hadn't picked it up in the sales. I felt like I needed to pay more. The game embraces gore and grittiness to create an overall depressing atmosphere for Miami in the 80's which compliments it's simple yet expansive story throughout. While the LSD-like retro graphics were strange for me at first, I quickly adapted to the style. The gameplay is fluent and a death rarely ever feels like you've been cheated by the game due to it's 'glass cannon' approach to combat. One hit to kill; one hit to die. While the constant appearence of 'press R to restart' made me want to gouge my eyes out due to the difficulty of this game at parts, I never once was turned off by it. If anything, it motivated me to play it more. While at first glance, the gameplay may seem to be another run 'n' gun scenario, it is far from that. Once again as a result of the one shot to kill scenario, you'll find yourself planning a route and stratagising how to take out the enimies in the area. Will you lure them over with gunshots or silently kill him from behind? It makes for a personalised experience. Overall, I would highly reccomend this game, A Steven Hawking/ Donald Trump.

A.	Introduction: Mafia 3 excels in exhibiting the south in during the 1960s though it’s well written characters and phenomenal performances can’t save this game from mediocrity.
B.	Gameplay: The core gameplay consists of standard third person shooting, gaining intel from local thugs, the occasional blowing up of things important to the mob you are trying to dismantle, such as, moonshine and ammo. You also assassinate some key members of the racket to draw out the person in charge of the racket, then you kill him and assign the racket to one of your business associates. You do this over and over and over again, until you are blue in the face. Eventually you will get a mission integral to the story which are fun but not enough to detract from the overly repetitive gameplay loop.
C.	Presentation: The game presents itself very well with some very impressive cut scenes and voice acting. The setting is an interesting place to inhabit, since there are not many games that take place in a New Orleans style city. While being interesting the world suffers from feeling a little empty and at times lifeless. The Music however both the licensed tracks and the original score really help in creating the sense of not only being in New Orleans but living in the 60s
D.	Narrative: It is important that I note that I did not finish the game due to the repetitive gameplay loop that I refuse to endure any longer, but from what I played the story seemed excellent and I genuinely started to care about Lincoln and his band of criminal misfits.
E.	Conclusion: The game ranges from fantastic to dismal and all in all is just a lot of wasted potential. Maybe next time around they should focus less on a ton of content to fill up time but rather focus on unique individual missions. The current main content feels like side content.

The Binding of Isaac is an amazing game that mixes elements from The Legend of Zelda dungeon crawling all the way to games like Minecraft with it's randomization. In the Binding of Isaac, you play as a small boy called, Issac who is chased down into the basement of his house due to his Mother believing that she is hearing the voice of God.
You can collect many different types of Weapons in the Binding of Isaac. Ranging from arrows, to bombs, to stranger things such as ipecac, to brimstone, to chocolate milk! There more items than just weapons. You can collect things that will aid you on your journey such as dog food (Additional health), and Pyro (You grow fuses in your head that give you 99 bombs). There is a great diversity of items in the game and it is very unlikely that you will get the same items in next playthroughs.
Now, all of these items don't mean much if the combat is bad. And it is not. Rooms are randomly generated and there is quite a selection of enemies to fight. All the enemies in the game serve a specific role to play. There are not many different types of bosses however in the game, which does mean that you repeat a boss that you fought in a previous run.
All in all, the binding of isaac is a great dungeon crawling game and plenty of randomization to make each run different.

No matter how good a story is in a game, you can't polish a turd.
Lets get the good bits out the way...:
- Story.
Yep thats about it...oh and maybe driving, maybe.
And now for the bad (inhales dramatically),
First 1hr 1/2 to 2hrs are actually quite polished, with interesting missions, story and gampley. But...once you are past the refund playtime the game takes a turn for the worse. Each story mission get basically locked until you do a bunch of side missions that have you sneaking or shooting through buildings to either steal, damage, interigate or kill a boss of that specific location. The downside to this is that no matter what one you are provided to complete, they all pretty much play out the same. By that I mean, kill a bunch of easy thugs, take the odd bit of dollar and if its a killing mission, get the boss. Once all of these specific side missions are done, your thugs move in and you assign a random guy to be the new "boss" of that group or racket as they are called.
With the limited combat options (I.e. press a button to stab, whistle them over to stab, or shoot them) the game gets very stale. I think the best part of the game apart from the story, is the driving. But after a while that too goes stale. Oh and get this, if you flip a car upside down, there is a button prompt that says (flip car) and the car then unrealistically just turns upright like nothing has happened lol.
Graphically the game is quite discusting. There is a constant moody/dull colour that lingers over the screen. Everything is very blury, no matter what graphical setting you are on. Not only that, a lot of objects have texture glitches were they disapeer or change colour, similar to gmod if you dont have a certain asset. The game also launched at 30fps which everyone now probably knows about, but when the 60fps patch finally appeared, even with a high end rig you could bearly run it @ 60fps.
This game is a huge mess and I feel robbed at £35, must be even more upsetting for those console users having to pay £49.99 0_0. But lets be honest, this game was rushed for consoles and then ported to PC.

Dont let you fool by the low Meta-Score:
SpellForce is a great game and a hidden gem, even more if you regard the price for the platinum edition.
It is by no means perfect, and can become really annoying at times, but it still is one of the best games i have played this year!
About pros and cons:
One the negative side, this game does neither feel like "real" role play nor like "deep" strategy.
The strategy part is extremely simple, without real tactics involved, and the role playing part leaves very little room for character developement.
Additionaly, the game gets repetetive, and at times, unfair, which means, that your main objectives  are, to defeat all opponents, which will produce endless units, the further you get the more, until you stop them.
And finally, theres a lack in comfort. Moving around a map is painfully slow, and every time you re-enter a map, you have to discover it anew.
On the positive side, theres a lenghty campaign (easily 100+ hours, if you plan to finish every quest in the game, which i strongly recommend), including a great and interesting story, different races with unique buildings and units, tons of side quests and stuff to explore, beautiful graphics and sound, great atmosphere, very intuitive controls, a great interface and a lot of fun!

tl;dr: Don't get this game.
I got this game a while back, about two years ago or so, as part of the Steam Summer Sale of that year. It was advertised as a hybrid RPG/RTS game, and since those are my two favorite genres, I thought it was a good deal. Boy, was I wrong. It turns out that when you try to serve two masters at once, you end up serving neither. This isn't a hybrid RPG/RTS game; it's a mediocre RPG duct taped to a mediocre RTS, resulting in a very boring a repetitive gameplay. Spellcasters in particular are annoying to level up, as you have to collect a spell once at its minimum level and for each level above it. The various stat requirements for combat and magic skills also punishes you for trying to be creative, as choosing skills with mismatched stat requirements will result in you never reaching the maximum level for one or both skills.
Graphics-wise, it has not aged well, as it dates to the time when 3D acceleration was in its infancy, and the graphics look primitive compared to its contemporary 2D or hybrid 2D/3D games. As for the audio, the voice acting is inconsistent. Some of the voice acting is professional, though done by voice actors who aren't native English speakers, which adds a dash of the exotic to the involved characters. The rest is terrible and amateurish, and ruins immersion when heard alongside the decent voice acting.

As an avid action gamer out there, I'd recommend this game for several reasons. While it isn't perfect, it does provide thrilling battles to say the very least. With all panty shots aside i'll begin with the pros.
Pros:
- Price point is 10$ , as an indie title that will occupy you for at least 5 hours assuming you're not a fighting god it was good. I bought it on a sale which sold at $2.50. Unbeatable.
- The simple graphical style is colorful, I personally enjoy the character models.
- Easy to dive into and have fun with.
- Great to play in short peroids of time
- Contains a unique objective in its combat that is original so far.
- Detailed animations that flows nicely in its combat.
Cons:
- The story is lacking depth, practically nonexistant.
- An underwelming amount of content. (Looks back at its price point..)
- This isn't an adventure game, and will isolate players on a very small plain each stage.
- Gameplay gets repetitive quickly , yes this game has Beat em' up syndrome too.
- Some unlockable skills will probably be tossed in the player's trash bin of unused skills.
This game isn't for everyone, espeically those who find displeasure in a game with very strict mechanics. The use of Just Guard, Parry, and Counters in the game leaves players with a tiny window to use. Some hardcore action gamers would adapt to such, but it is difficult for people to make use of in general. Enemies attacks have priority over the player's, meaning if an enemy is attacking you aren't... unless you're some hotshot who is very good at judging the frames on attacks. While I personally see a lot of potential in its combat, it does not hold up as a novel or an exploration simulator it does make a fun, rewarding hack and slash game in my humble opinion. 7/10

What makes this game so disappointingly bad is not all of its bad qualities, but all the good ideas that were executed poorly.

Unfortunately, the problems this game has will make you forget those things. The shakicam is very disorienting, both during combat and when trying to figure out where to go (a strangely common problem in a linear cover shooter). Furthermore, the actual combat is too basic and the enemies don't really change besides what they are using. Lastly, all the automatic weapons have terrible recoil and spread, which makes the rifles and shotguns the weapons of choice.
Lastly, the game is short. It took my friend and I 3 hours to complete it on Medium. It's not worth buying even on a sale.

Broken Age is a very pretty game in terms of visuals and audio. The story is incredibly creative and enjoyable; it really is unimaginable how Tim Schafer came up with some of these ideas. The writing also made the experience a whole lot more enjoyable - and when combined with the voice acting and visuals, the characters became outstandingly vibrant and believable.
That being said, the game definitely isn't faultless; the puzzles are, as a whole, decent.
There are plenty of puzzles that are memorable, plenty that make sense, and plenty that are intuitive (to an appropriate extent) but rarely is there a puzzle which hits all these marks. The second act seems to be especially guilty of this, with quite a few puzzles that I reckon could've used some tinkering.
Despite this, I actually highly recommend this game. The puzzle issues may seem like a turn-off, but ultimately it's a very pleasant adventure of a game and definitely worth a try - besides, you can always look up solutions if you absolutely need to.

This game is perfect for those who love 2D side scrollers with deathmatch added to it. In it, you can have a match with up to 4 people and be on teams or play free for all. You spawn in randomly in a small map that you can see all the time and you need to find weapons in '!' blocks. Obviously once you find a weapon, you need to go find your target. Each round lasts about 20 seconds (because 1 hit = insta death unless you find armor). The goal is to get the most points by the end of the game. Not to mention therer is hats. You can either unlock hats, download them from the Workshop, or make your own and share it with friends. Also, there is a level editor. Once you finished your level, you can upload it to the workshop just like you can with hats. I usually play about 100 rounds before taking a break when playing this game, and just because the rounds are short doesn't mean you will get bored quicker. Its just fast pace, where you want to play your cards right and avoid anything that can kill you. Did I mention that there is a mind control weapon located in certain maps? It lets you take control of your opponent if you can manage to sap them with the beams and make them jump off a cliff. I did this and managed to make 3 of the other ducks drop their weapons and walk off cliffs. This is unique and coded very nicely. Each time I launch it I notice I burn a few hours of my day away on it. Lastly, there is arcade. Just a place where you can go pratice your skills on non-moving ducks. Over all, this is a great game.

Have a few minutes before class? Waiting for in a lobby of a multiplayer game with nothing to do? The Binding of Isaac is the perfect game for those times when you want a bit of challenge and a deep game to play without committing too much time.
Synopsis: The Binding of Isaac revolves around an unclothed child by the name of Isaac, who flees to a basement filled with monsters to escape his mother who is trying to kill him as an offering to God. To escape, he must fight through rooms of enemies using his tears as a weapon. There are also random items throughout the game to help (or hinder) Isaac’s journey, hidden in rooms or in piles of poop.  Sound weird enough?
Gameplay: The Binding of Isaac is a 2D top-down perspective where each screen is a room of the basement. Think of the classic Legend of Zelda’s dungeons for reference. The basement is broken up by floors (or levels) with multiple rooms on each floor. In some rooms there are randomly chosen items you can pick up that can affect the game. Some items can be used throughout the game as weapons, while other upgrade or downgrade Isaac’s stats (.i.e. How fast he can shoot/move/range). Here in lies the true reason for the replay value of the game is so high and frustration level can equal that. While there are websites that can tell you what each item does, without looking at them there are items that can punish a first time player for using or picking up. I personally have 130 deaths and have only beaten the game twice. It does get easier as I understand how to use the items, but I feel its cheating to use guides that tell me what each do.
Positive:
+Randomly spawned enemies and items give the game a high replay value.
+Game can be played in a short amount of time.
+Rewards multiple playthrough as you can better understand the enemy’s patterns.
Negative
-Some Items have negative effects, which is a “noob trap” that punishes new players.
-No save feature included
Art Style/Graphics:  The art style can be defined as both gruesomely violent and beautiful, with a slight feeling of nostalgia. Made by one of the same developers of Super Meat Boy, the graphics and art direction borrow a lot from the NES generation and expands upon it with dark humor. The Binding of Isaac goes the extra mile in designing enemies, as each feels unique and original. The game also has the options of playing the game in full screen or windowed mode at multiple resolutions. This makes it so it can be played on almost any computer regardless of the graphics card.
Positive:
+Enemies are original and unique.
+Can be played on lower-end computers.
Negative:
-Can be gross at times.
Soundtrack/Sound effects: This will probably the shortest part of the review because I really can’t say anything bad about it. The soundtrack stands on its own and worth the purchase with or without the game. I would play this game in-between matches of League of Legends and leave the game open just listen to the music. Like all games, it can become repetitive if overdone.
Cost: The cost of the game is the real reason I wanted to write this review. I own close to 100 games on steam and The Binding of Isaac is the game I have logged the most hours. I purchased this game during a steam sale for $1 and I can easily say it is worth the money. Being a 25 year old college student with a wife and apartment, it was probably the $1 I could have spent on leisure. This game was also included in a recent humble bundle with 5+ other games for $6.50. They did add DLC for a small amount (maybe $3), but I’m in the boat that thinks games should be released when ready and left to stand on its own.
Positive:
+Very inexpensive
Negative:
-(Personal View) DLC

You will often find, among gamers and critics alike, diverse opinions that state the positives and negatives of various games, with things such as "the game is good" or "the game was too short" or "the controls suck."
This is not the case with Dust: An Elysian Tail.  I have been a gamer my entire life, ostracized as a child in school by the very people now addicted to Call of Duties and Madden NFLs.  I have watched the evolution of gaming from the 8-and-16-bit era of Mario and Sonic, the evolution of PC gaming from text based RPGs to DragonAge and Skyrim.
Of all the games I have played, from casual Runescape to the intensely cerebral Europa Universalis, from the flashy twitch gaming of Smash Brothers to the thought-out fights of Guild Wars.  "Dust: An Elysian Tail" is by far one of the most defining creations in the Gaming Industry.  What makes it more spectacular and amazing is the story of a single man hand-drawing and developing the game from scratch over years, of an indie developer given a chance on Xbox Arcade.
Dead Dodrill has brought to us a game that, in collaboration with secondary writer Alex Kain, and composers Alexander Brandon and HypderDuck Soundworks, defines everything we love about gaming.  He brings us back to the core elements of a video game.
I can say, without a doubt in my mind, that Dust: An Elysian Tail is, by far, the greatest representation of Video Games as an Artform.  If there ever any confusion or concern if games could be consider Art, Dead Dodrill has proved us otherwise.
No amount of praise I could give would satisfy my love for this game.  For 17 years, Blizzard Entertainment's Starcraft franchise has held a special place in my heart as my favorite game of all time.  Upon completion of this artistic masterwork, I can say that this has changed.
Dean Dodrill, Alexander Brandon, and everyone else that not only made this game possible, but brought it to the attention of the general public.  I thank you, and I heartily reccommend this game for anyone.

A fun open-world game marred by technical issues and repetitive mission structure. The base for the game itself is great, but it definitely needed more time in development before it released and it really shows. With a few updates involving customization, optimization, and more graphics options I believe we could see the game become a bit above average, but without these things it's an average game with a great story and interesting characters. You'll want to keep playing to learn more about the world and story of Lincoln Clay, but you'll have to slog through the choppiness to get to it. The gunplay and driving (core elements of the game) are excellent and feel good, but the "go here, destroy stuff, lure out boss" style of missions that take place in every district so far have been less than amazing.
Overall if I had to give it an arbitrary number rating, it'd be a 7 or 7.5/10 for me.

Little did i know the hole goes to China. 90% of the time, i prefer long games, makes the experience lasting and fun to view in scope. However, games that i tend to enjoy that last upwards 100 hours usually have meat in them, every minute is either action packed or planning. This game is not one of those games. I dont know how many collective hours i spent READING A BOOK while waiting for characters to travel across the map because of poor quest design and placements of locations. Sadly there is no speed adjustment, and each map you play on can last upwards 3-4 hours, which really emphasizes placing content in the map itself, whereas  you forget a chest that might have something nice inside, you have a 8 minute jog all the way back to it, and then another 8 minutes back to a bindstone or portal. The bindstones are your only salvation to get across some of these huge maps with empty space, but even then they are few and far between. I beat the main campaign lasted about 70 hours, got into the 2nd campaign and almost got to the end. Game crashed, and after getting back in found that the autosave feature apparently decided that 4 hours worth of gameplay wasnt worth saving in between. Ive given up, especially knowing that there are many other games out there that want attention. This isnt some Grand Strategy game that requires patience, its an RTS that either moves too slow or has maps way too big. Maybe when i have nothing else, I'll come back to finish, but 100 hours of the SAME BORING GRIND and all i really want to do is just move on. Spellforce, take a few lessons from Warcraft 3. Mafia 3 starts out with a big bang, a nice intro, Netflix-style documentary cutscenes and then puts you right in to a heist job. Some great 60s music playing as you're getting chased by cops on a boat full of cash and you're thinking "Damn this is good, I can tell this game is going to get good". It does not get good. It get's repetitive.
While the voice acting, the animation, capturing the feel of the 60s is top notch, the gameplay is probably this game's major fault aside from the technical issues. Once you get past those, you realise how boring and repetitive missions can be. Was I playing a side mission? No, it was part of the whole story mission, a mission that you needed to do in order to progress.
Step 1 : Shoot guys, interrogate their leader, kill or recruit him,
Step 2 : Do enough of this till someone tells you the leader of the district is out of hiding and killable
Step 3 : Kill said leader, give district to one of your three underbosses.
Repeat.
There really isn't much variety here and it pains me to see the Mafia series taking this direction. Stop trying to be GTA and  go back to being what Mafia was about. A story-driven game with an open world that keeps it's focus on the story.
Where are the awesome minute details we've seen in Mafia 1 and 2?
Why aren't police giving us tickets anymore and instead just shooting us if we rammed our car into someone else?
Why can't I turn lights on and off, turn on the shower, have a place to sleep, eat and drink to replenish my health?
The game becomes more of a chore to finish now though the only motivation to completing the game is just to see the story progress, although to be honest, it's a predictable story (Guy loses everything, guy builds up his arsenal to get revenge on baddie, guy kills said baddie, everyone happily skips into the horizon, the end). In Mafia 1 and 2, it felt more like it had inspiration from Godfather and Goodfellas, one of the best gangster movies out there ever, where we couldn't see what the outcome of the ending was going to be, the story just unravels itself along the way.
The characters in this game are set up quite well, don't get me wrong, but later on you can feel like you know what will happen next and that's not something you'd want to know.
Mafia 3? More like Mafia Pee.
